text:
maya: Quick sketch — proposing a "compatibility preview" in the routing console so devs can see which models a given rule will select and why.
ryan: +1. We keep getting support tickets where routes pin to a quantized variant that lacks streaming or KV behavior.
sam: Important: preview should surface capability mismatches (KV cache, streaming, tokenizer differences) not just alias matches.
anita: Also need cost/latency projections. Ops cares about 99p latency when a large model gets pinned.
maya: Example rule I was thinking of:
```
route {
  match: header("x-rl-route") == "payments"
  require: model.capabilities.contains("kv-cache") && model.max_seq >= 4096
  pin: alias("payments-encoder")
  fallback: [alias("payments-encoder-v1"), tag("fallback-lowcost")]
}
```
maya: The preview would evaluate that rule against our catalog and show: matched models, reason for exclusion, estimated 95/99th latency, and token cost.
ryan: How do we compute 'estimated latency' without running per-model perf tests for all combinations? That's expensive.
sam: We can use telemetry + model profiles. We already have per-model seq-length latency curves from Benchmark infra.
anita: Concern: header overrides from customer side (x-model-alias) might bypass console guardrails. Should gateway accept direct alias headers or only allow an allowlist per-route?
maya: I think default should be reject unless tenant explicitly opts in. Otherwise customers can bypass compatibility checks.
ryan: Agreed. Also add a flag to the rule: allow_user_overrides: false/true.
sam: UX: show a clear yellow warning if a rule's fallback includes models with weaker guarantees (no streaming, lower tokenization fidelity).
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: routing-console/compat-preview v0.1 -> staging at 2025-07-12T09:00Z :rocket:
anita: Edge case: model groups - e.g., alias("embedder-*") that expands to multiple families. The preview should summarize groups, not list dozens of variants.
maya: Implementation notes: a backend evaluator that runs rule expressions against model metadata (capabilities, tags, perf profiles). It needs caching and a way to mark snapshot time for audit.
ryan: Can we reuse the existing routing-eval library? It already supports header expressions and pins but not capability predicates.
sam: Slight API change: add a new predicate 'model.supports("kv-cache")' and normalized capability set in model metadata.
anita: One last ask: telemetry link from preview to 'what happened' in prod (show recent route hit logs where rule matched and which fallback executed).
maya: I'll put together a PR for the console mockups + evaluator spec. tagging @ryan @sam for review. :thumbsup:
ryan: Sounds good — will review tomorrow.
sam: lgtm
